mission_context: NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Landing Site
scientific_summary: A 49-km impact crater that hosted a prominent open-basin lake fed by two inlet valleys during the Noachian-Hesperian transition (~3.7 Ga). Features a remarkably preserved fluvial delta with clay, carbonate, and olivine-bearing strata. Contains ground-truth environmental measurements from the Perseverance MEDA instrument suite.
geological_epoch: Circa 3.7 Ga (Late Noachian to Early Hesperian)

coordinates.datum: MOLA areoid (0 m elevation defined at mean radius 3396.0 km)

elevation.name: surface_elevation
elevation.instrument: MOLA / HiRISE DTM / Perseverance MEDA barometer
elevation.citation: Farley et al. (2020), Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. (2021)
elevation.notes: Elevation of floor and western delta fan base

slope.name: crater_floor_slope
slope.instrument: HiRISE DTM / Rover IMU traversability logs
slope.notes: Landing ellipse is flat (1.5 deg), delta scarp exceeds 15-20 deg

surface_roughness_rms.name: decameter_rms_roughness
surface_roughness_rms.instrument: HiRISE / Perseverance Navcam stereo point clouds
surface_roughness_rms.notes: Moderate-to-high roughness due to fractured floor (Séítah) and boulder ejecta

temperature_mean_annual.name: surface_temperature_annual_mean
temperature_mean_annual.notes: Ground-truth calibrated surface temperature from rover

temperature_diurnal_range.name: diurnal_temperature_amplitude
temperature_diurnal_range.notes: Extreme diurnal swing between afternoon peak and pre-dawn minimum

thermal_inertia.name: thermal_inertia
thermal_inertia.instrument: THEMIS Mosaic / MEDA derived surface thermal inertia
thermal_inertia.notes: Higher than Oxia Planum due to exposed olivine-cumulate bedrock and coarse sand dunes

albedo_bolometric.name: bolometric_visible_albedo
albedo_bolometric.notes: Dark Séítah unit has albedo ~0.11; delta top has albedo ~0.18

clay_phyllosilicate_index.name: delta_smectite_carbonate_absorption
clay_phyllosilicate_index.citation: Ehlmann et al. (2008), Farley et al. (2022)
clay_phyllosilicate_index.notes: Localized in western delta fan mudstones and crater marginal carbonates

water_equivalent_hydrogen.name: water_equivalent_hydrogen_weh
water_equivalent_hydrogen.instrument: Mars Odyssey GRS / HEND Neutron Spectrometer
water_equivalent_hydrogen.notes: Chemically bound within delta clays and hydrated sulfates

atmospheric_pressure.name: mean_surface_pressure
atmospheric_pressure.notes: Measured ground-truth pressure at Jezero floor (~7.1 hPa)

irreducible_limits.surface_gravity: Mars = 3.71 m/s^2 vs Earth = 9.81 m/s^2. Sediment settling velocity in paleolake deltas was significantly lower on Mars.
irreducible_limits.radiation_environment: Surface dose at Jezero measured by MEDA/RAD analogs is ~240-260 mSv/yr.
irreducible_limits.biological_sterility: Jezero delta on Earth would be saturated with microbial mats and plant roots; Martian delta is pristine abiotic rock.

recommended_earth_analog_archetypes: Green River Formation (Utah/Wyoming) - Lacustrine carbonate and deltaic facies
Lake Eyre Basin (Australia) - Arid terminal lake delta and clay playa
